artifact: SFEB MON-005 durable SQLite witness reference model v1
sqlite_witness_backend: Node.js node:sqlite; file-backed per-witness state; DELETE journal; synchronous=FULL; BEGIN IMMEDIATE
sqlite_cases: checkpoint and challenge signature persist across closing and reopening database handles
lost acknowledgement after COMMIT recovers the exact durable signature after reopening
pre-commit fault rolls back both witness head and challenge receipt
competing writer fails closed while another connection holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then succeeds after release
runtime_warning: Node.js emitted ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature and might change at any time.
limitations: the four witness instances and their SQLite databases are exercised within one process and one host; independent hosts or administrative failure domains are not demonstrated
close/reopen is same-process database-handle restart simulation, not an independently spawned process, power-loss, filesystem-corruption, or hardware fault test
SQLite synchronous=FULL and DELETE journal settings are configured but do not constitute verified power-loss or storage-device durability evidence
test keys are deterministic fixtures, not production keys or HSM-backed identities
canonicalization is a strict local JSON subset, not a complete RFC 8785 implementation
the witness model has no network protocol, PostgreSQL adapter, trusted timestamp authority, production key rotation/revocation, or hardware isolation
proof bundle generation still receives the full local log array; witness verification consumes only the new suffix plus consistency and inclusion proofs
no real external mutation sink, sink-side objective-fence enforcement, or independent postcondition readback is implemented
